x.section: Recommendation 2.10; Figure 2.1 footnote 2

x.note: A NEGATIVE antibody does not refute type 1: about 65% of young clinically diagnosed type 1 in Cameroon, Uganda and South Africa was antibody negative. ADA's statement that a negative result 'does not change the diagnosis' is limited to people diagnosed under 35 with no features of type 2 or monogenic diabetes.

heldOut.why: Only the high criterion stays out. ADA 2026 Fig. 2.1: 600 pmol/L or more after more than 3 years, antibody negative, aged 35 or over, reads as type 2. The runtime reads supporting criteria only, so a refuting one needs an engine change; its only use would be to argue against type 1, which the pack never acts on (it never proposes stopping insulin).

citation.title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026
citation.quote: If the result is ≥600 pmol/L (≥1.8 ng/mL), the circumstances of testing do not matter. If the result is <600 pmol/L (<1.8 ng/mL) and the concurrent glucose is <4 mmol/L (<70 mg/dL) or the person may have been fasting, consider repeating the test. Results showing very low levels (e.g., <80 pmol/L [<0.24 ng/mL]) do not need to be repeated.
citation.needsCsoInput: 600 pmol/L is printed in the figure legend as the level above which 'the circumstances of testing do not matter'. The statement that it strongly suggests type 2 diabetes is inside the flowchart image (Holt 2021 Fig. 1; ADA 2026 Fig. 2.1), which could not be read. A person must read the figure before any rule uses it.

x.section: Figure 2.1 footnotes 4 and 9 (flowchart for investigation of suspected type 1 diabetes in newly diagnosed adults)

x.caveat: ADA 2026 Fig. 2.1 is based on data from White European adults. Ketosis-prone diabetes, common in Africa, can show a low C-peptide soon after ketoacidosis; the 2-week rule guards only part of that.
x.ug2026: 2026 diagnoses type 1 on '≥2 islet-cell autoantibodies' (p. 60). Not required here (UG-14, CSO): antibodies are rarely available and often negative in Ugandan type 1; insulin and ketone education never wait on the test.

rules.notes: The count of two is this pack's, not the source's: ADA/EASD says only that no single feature confirms type 1, and its figure is drawn from White European data. rules.notes: WHO lists 'clinical suspicion of type 1 diabetes in newly diagnosed patient' for same-day referral. The classic fatal error is the thin young adult labelled type 2, sent home on tablets and back in ketoacidosis. The count of two is this pack's (D-DM-10). The rule writes no type. The rule reads the glucose itself, so it does not wait for the criteria set, which may be waiting on the pregnancy answer.

proposal.then: refer the same day if type 1 is suspected
